definitionEn: A man who rules a country and is the head of its royal family.
example: The king ordered the building of a great stone castle on the hill.

definitionEn: A woman who rules a country and is the head of its royal family.
example: The queen visited the village to celebrate the anniversary of the battle.

definitionEn: A state of armed conflict between countries or groups.
example: The war lasted six years and destroyed many farms and villages.

definitionEn: A fight between armed forces during a war, usually in one place.
example: The battle at the river turned the course of the entire campaign.

definitionEn: A large stone building with thick walls, built for defence in the past.
example: Visitors climb the narrow stairs of the castle to see the view.

definitionEn: A person who serves in an army, especially in its ordinary ranks.
example: The young soldier wrote letters home every week during the long campaign.

definitionEn: A ruler of an empire, often holding more power than a king.
example: The emperor ordered new roads to be built across the vast territory.

definitionEn: A country ruled by a king or queen.
example: The small kingdom grew rich from trade along the coast road.

definitionEn: A person who has power to govern a country or region.
example: The wise ruler listened to advisers before making any major decision.

definitionEn: A period when there is no war between countries or groups.
example: The treaty brought peace to the region after decades of fighting.

definitionEn: A period of one hundred years.
example: Many historic buildings in the old town date from the eighteenth century.

definitionEn: A large group of countries or territories ruled by one leader or government.
example: The empire stretched from the mountains in the north to the sea.

definitionEn: A small group of houses in a rural area, smaller than a town.
example: Our grandparents lived in a small village near the rice fields.

definitionEn: A person in your family who lived in the past and from whom you are descended.
example: Our ancestors farmed this land for many generations before us.

definitionEn: The study of past events, or the record of those events.
example: She loves reading about the history of ancient trade routes.

definitionEn: The time before the present, or events that have already happened.
example: Many people enjoy learning about the past through old photographs and letters.

definitionEn: Something you remember from earlier times in your life.
example: My earliest memory is of a village festival with lanterns and music.

definitionEn: A building where objects of historical, scientific, or artistic interest are displayed.
example: The museum displays tools and pottery that were found at the site.

definitionEn: A book in which a person writes about daily events and personal thoughts.
example: The soldier's diary describes the cold winter nights spent in the trenches.

definitionEn: To find something that was hidden or unknown before.
example: Archaeologists discovered a set of coins buried beneath the old floor.

definitionEn: A person who travels to unknown places in order to learn about them.
example: The explorer sailed across the ocean in search of a new trade route.

definitionEn: The act of entering a country by force with an army to take control.
example: The invasion of the island began at dawn with a surprise landing.

definitionEn: A formal written agreement between two or more countries or states.
example: The treaty ended the long conflict and established new borders for both nations.

definitionEn: A territory controlled by another country and settled by its people.
example: The colony gained independence after decades of protest and negotiation.

definitionEn: An organised attempt by a group of people to overthrow those in power.
example: The revolt spread quickly from the capital to the surrounding provinces.

definitionEn: To take control of a country or territory by force.
example: The army hoped to conquer the northern valleys before the winter arrived.

definitionEn: A formal agreement between countries or groups to work together for a shared purpose.
example: The alliance between the two kingdoms lasted for more than a century.

definitionEn: A system of government with a king or queen as head of state.
example: Many European countries still keep a monarchy, though it has limited power.

definitionEn: A member of the highest social class, often holding land and inherited titles.
example: The aristocrat invited scholars and artists to his grand estate each summer.

definitionEn: A poor farmer or worker in a traditional rural society.
example: Peasants worked the fields for landowners and paid heavy taxes each harvest.

definitionEn: The arrangement of events or dates in the order in which they happened.
example: The historian arranged the letters in chronology to show how the crisis developed.

definitionEn: A place where people have come to live and build homes, often newly established.
example: The early settlement grew into a busy town beside the river.

definitionEn: A change made to improve a system, especially a political or social one.
example: The reform of the tax system reduced poverty among rural families.

definitionEn: To officially end a law, custom, or institution.
example: The parliament voted to abolish slavery throughout the empire.

definitionEn: The development of large-scale manufacturing in an economy or region.
example: Rapid industrialisation transformed the countryside into a series of factory towns.

definitionEn: The growing movement of people from rural areas into cities.
example: Urbanisation brought new jobs but also overcrowded housing to the city.

definitionEn: To dig carefully in order to uncover buried remains or objects.
example: Teams excavated the ruins over several summers to reveal the old palace.

definitionEn: Relating to or inherited from one's ancestors.
example: The family returned to their ancestral village to restore the old house.

definitionEn: The preserved remains or impression of a plant or animal from long ago, found in rock.
example: Scientists found a fossil of a fish that lived millions of years ago.

definitionEn: A book or document written by hand, especially before printing existed.
example: The monks copied each manuscript carefully by hand in the candlelit library.

definitionEn: A long roll of paper or parchment on which writing is recorded.
example: The scholar unrolled the fragile scroll to read its faded characters.

definitionEn: A gradual loss of strength, power, or importance over time.
example: The decline of the empire began when its armies lost key battles abroad.

definitionEn: A sudden, organised rising of people against authority.
example: The uprising against the governor spread from village to village in spring.

definitionEn: Dominance of one state or group over others, especially in political or economic control.
example: The empire maintained its hegemony over the region through trade and alliances.

meaningVi: phong trào nổi dậy vũ trang
definitionEn: An armed rebellion against an established government by an organised group.
example: The insurgency spread through the mountains, where government troops struggled to respond.

definitionEn: The act of forcibly taking control of a territory and adding it to another state.
example: The annexation of the border province provoked fierce protests in the capital.

definitionEn: A system of government in which one person holds absolute power.
example: Under the dictatorship, newspapers were censored and dissent was harshly punished.

definitionEn: The act of freeing a person or group from legal, social, or political restrictions.
example: The emancipation of enslaved people transformed the social order of the region.

definitionEn: The right to vote in political elections.
example: The campaign for women's suffrage lasted decades before reaching final success.

definitionEn: A system of administration run by officials, often criticised for its complexity.
example: The bureaucracy of the late empire grew so large that decisions were slow.

definitionEn: The supreme authority of a state to govern itself without outside interference.
example: The treaty recognised the sovereignty of the new republic over its borders.

definitionEn: A system of ideas and beliefs that shapes the political or economic goals of a group.
example: The movement's ideology promised equality, but it demanded total loyalty from members.

definitionEn: Information, often biased, spread to promote a political cause or damage an opponent.
example: Wartime propaganda posters urged citizens to work harder for the nation.

definitionEn: Arranged in the order in which events occurred in time.
example: The museum displays its exhibits in strict chronological order from oldest to newest.

definitionEn: A collection of historical documents or records kept for reference.
example: Researchers spent months in the national archive studying wartime letters.

definitionEn: Relating to archives or the records kept in them.
example: The historian made an important archival discovery in a dusty attic.

meaningVi: tường thuật, câu chuyện lịch sử
definitionEn: A spoken or written account of connected events, presented as a story.
example: The author's narrative of the revolution reflects only one side of events.

definitionEn: An earlier event or thing that comes before and resembles a later one.
example: Its antecedents can be traced back to the reforms of the previous century.

definitionEn: An earlier event or decision that serves as an example or guide for later ones.
example: The judges followed a precedent set by their predecessors a century earlier.

definitionEn: The rebuilding of something destroyed, or a recreation of past events or appearance.
example: The reconstruction of the city after the war took nearly two decades.

definitionEn: The division of history into distinct periods or eras for study.
example: Periodisation of the past can be controversial, since historians disagree on dates.

definitionEn: Relating to the structure and statistics of a population, such as age or sex.
example: The demographic changes after the famine altered the size of the workforce.

definitionEn: The mass departure of many people from a place, usually because of difficulty.
example: The exodus from the drought-stricken valley left few families in the village.

meaningVi: cộng đồng người sống xa quê hương
definitionEn: A community of people who have spread away from their original homeland.
example: The diaspora kept its language and traditions alive for several generations abroad.

definitionEn: A social system in which lords granted land to vassals in exchange for loyalty and service.
example: Feudalism shaped rural life across Europe for several centuries of the middle ages.

definitionEn: An economic policy aiming to increase national wealth through trade and colonies.
example: Mercantilism encouraged rulers to export goods and accumulate gold and silver.

definitionEn: The principle that government and public institutions should be separate from religion.
example: Secularism became a central principle of the new constitution after the revolution.

definitionEn: Strong loyalty to one's own nation, sometimes leading to rivalry with others.
example: Rising nationalism fuelled tensions between the neighbouring countries before the war.

definitionEn: The policy of extending a nation's power over other lands through conquest or trade.
example: Imperialism brought railways and schools, but also exploitation and resistance.

definitionEn: The act of surrendering or giving in to an enemy on agreed terms.
example: The general's capitulation ended the siege after three bitter months.

definitionEn: To give formal approval to a treaty, agreement, or law so that it becomes official.
example: The parliament refused to ratify the agreement until every clause was revised.

definitionEn: Strong disagreement with an official policy or with the views of a majority.
example: Public dissent grew louder as the government ignored the petitions of farmers.

meaningVi: chế độ nghĩa vụ quân sự
definitionEn: Compulsory enlistment of people into military service by law.
example: Conscription forced thousands of young men to leave their farms for the front.

definitionEn: A small remaining trace of something that has largely disappeared.
example: Only a few vestiges of the old fortress survive among the modern buildings.

definitionEn: Up until the present time, or until the point being discussed.
example: The region had hitherto been ignored by the central government in the capital.

definitionEn: The position of dominance or superior power over others.
example: The family's ascendancy in local politics lasted almost a century.

definitionEn: The process by which colonies gained independence from their former ruling powers.
example: Decolonisation in the region brought independence, but also new political struggles.

definitionEn: A group of soldiers stationed in a town or fort to defend it.
example: The garrison held the walls for six weeks despite constant bombardment.

definitionEn: An organised armed uprising against a government or ruler.
example: The insurrection in the south was crushed after several bloody months of fighting.

definitionEn: Relating to the common people, as opposed to the aristocracy, especially in ancient Rome.
example: The plebeian assembly gained new rights after years of protest against the senators.

meaningVi: bản thảo xoá đi viết lại
definitionEn: A manuscript on which earlier writing has been scraped away and overwritten.
example: Scholars used imaging to read the faint text hidden beneath a palimpsest.

definitionEn: A book printed in Europe before 1501, in the early days of printing.
example: The library's incunabulum contains woodcut illustrations printed before 1500.

meaningVi: tiểu sử ca ngợi quá đáng
definitionEn: A biography that idealises its subject, presenting them as flawless.
example: The hagiography omitted the ruler's cruelty and showed only his piety.

definitionEn: Writings of doubtful authenticity that were excluded from an accepted canon.
example: Historians debate whether the apocrypha contains genuine traditions about the early saints.

definitionEn: The study of ancient and medieval handwriting and writing systems.
example: Her training in palaeography allowed her to read the faded medieval charters.

definitionEn: The branch of geology concerned with layers of rock and soil and their dating.
example: Stratigraphy showed that the pottery belonged to a much earlier settlement.

definitionEn: The study or collection of coins, medals, and paper money.
example: Her interest in numismatics began when she found an old coin in the garden.

definitionEn: The study of inscriptions carved or written on durable surfaces such as stone.
example: Epigraphy helped scholars decipher the messages carved into the temple walls.

definitionEn: The theory and method of interpreting texts, especially historical or sacred ones.
example: Modern hermeneutics asks how the reader's own context shapes understanding of a text.

definitionEn: The explanation of events by reference to a predetermined purpose or goal.
example: Some older histories fall into teleology by presenting the past as leading inevitably to progress.

definitionEn: A narrative device that describes an event before it happens in the story's timeline.
example: The novelist used prolepsis to reveal the outcome of the war in the opening chapter.

definitionEn: Something placed in the wrong historical period, appearing out of its proper time.
example: The film contains an anachronism: a wristwatch that was not invented until later.

definitionEn: An ancient writing system made of wedge-shaped marks pressed into clay tablets.
example: Scribes recorded trade accounts in cuneiform on clay tablets thousands of years ago.

definitionEn: A writing material made from the pith of a reed, used in ancient Egypt and beyond.
example: The scribe wrote the decree on papyrus, rolling each sheet carefully when finished.

definitionEn: A fine material made from calfskin, used for manuscripts before paper became common.
example: The monks inked their prayers onto vellum that had been carefully scraped and smoothed.

definitionEn: A room in a monastery where monks copied and decorated manuscripts.
example: Each day the monks worked in the scriptorium, copying texts by candlelight.

definitionEn: A mound of earth or stones built over a grave or burial chamber.
example: Archaeologists opened the tumulus and found the bronze weapons buried inside.

definitionEn: An ancient burial mound, often covering a tomb or chamber.
example: Local children were told never to climb the barrow on the windy hill.

definitionEn: A pile of stones built as a memorial or marker, often on a hill or grave.
example: Walkers added a stone to the cairn as a sign of respect for the fallen.

definitionEn: A very large stone used alone or as part of a prehistoric monument.
example: Each megalith in the circle was dragged there by hand from distant quarries.

definitionEn: A prehistoric tomb made of large upright stones supporting a flat horizontal stone.
example: The dolmen stands alone in the field, its capstone balanced on two upright slabs.

definitionEn: An upright stone slab or pillar, often carved with inscriptions or images.
example: A stele engraved with the king's laws was placed in the temple courtyard.

definitionEn: A tall, four-sided stone pillar that tapers to a pyramid shape at the top.
example: The obelisk in the square was erected to honour the city's founding.

definitionEn: A stone coffin, often decorated with carvings and placed above ground.
example: Inside the sarcophagus, archaeologists discovered jewellery and a carved wooden mask.

definitionEn: A grand tomb or building constructed to house the remains of a notable person.
example: The emperor's mausoleum was surrounded by gardens and tall cypress trees.

definitionEn: A gap or missing portion, especially in a manuscript or in the historical record.
example: The lacuna in the chronicle leaves historians guessing about the king's final years.

definitionEn: A critical explanation or interpretation of a text, especially scripture.
example: Her exegesis of the ancient law code revealed several contradictory passages.

definitionEn: Relating to the underworld or gods of the earth, especially in ancient Greek religion.
example: Ancient Greeks made offerings to chthonic deities in pits dug into the earth.

definitionEn: The study of the causes of something, or the origin of a custom or event.
example: The historian's aetiology of the revolution emphasised economic hardship and debt.

definitionEn: A complicated and embarrassing situation, especially a confusing disagreement.
example: The diplomatic imbroglio over the border dragged on for several years.

definitionEn: Aggressive patriotism that favours war or threats against other nations.
example: Jingoism swept the newspapers as public anger over the crisis grew.

definitionEn: Excessive pride or self-confidence that leads a ruler or hero toward disaster.
example: The general's hubris led him to attack an army far stronger than his own.

definitionEn: A person or thing that brings about the downfall of a rival, or an unbeatable opponent.
example: For the king, the rebel leader became a lifelong nemesis and eventual conqueror.

definitionEn: To defeat an enemy completely in a battle or contest.
example: The coalition hoped to vanquish the invaders before the autumn rains began.

definitionEn: Eager or quick to start a war or to pick fights with others.
example: The bellicose ruler ignored his advisers and declared war on his neighbours.

definitionEn: A painting made on wet plaster on a wall or ceiling, so the colours soak into the surface.
example: The chapel's fresco shows saints and angels painted across its vaulted ceiling.

definitionEn: A picture or pattern made of small pieces of coloured stone, glass, or tile.
example: A mosaic of blue and gold tiles covered the floor of the ancient bathhouse.

definitionEn: A tomb, especially one cut from rock or built of stone.
example: Visitors leaned over the sepulchre to read the name carved upon its lid.

definitionEn: A sculpted or carved image of a person, often placed on a tomb.
example: The knight's stone effigy lies atop the tomb with his hands clasped in prayer.

definitionEn: A decorative band of carved or painted figures running along the upper part of a wall.
example: A carved frieze of soldiers marching wraps around the top of the temple.
